lead.title: MintNeuro (Imperial College spin-off) raises $5M led by Odyssey Ventures for chips built for neural implants
lead.deck: The UK startup is building a modular semiconductor platform (neural sensing, signal processing, stimulation) for implants and wearables; 33East, JSK Investments, Alumni Ventures and returning backers Empirical Ventures and Jumpspace Ventures complete the round. Proceeds fund engineering and commercial hiring and a US presence: a picks-and-shovels play in neurotech, upstream of the devices themselves.

milestone.title: Science Corporation: PRIMA subretinal implant gains an average of 29 letters at 36 months in geographic atrophy
milestone.summary: In the PRIMAvera study, 14 of 18 evaluable patients gain at least 15 letters and natural vision stays stable; no new safety signal between 12 and 36 months (presented at EURETINA, Vienna, Oct 1–4). PRIMA is available in Europe and the UK and remains under FDA review.
milestone.why: Three-year durability in a condition with no vision-restoring treatment strengthens the retinal prosthesis thesis and sets up the FDA decision, a key catalyst for the segment.

brefsEurope.title: Cambridge Heartwear wins a £184M NHS Supply Chain tender for its HeartSense ECG monitor
brefsEurope.summary: The AI-driven wearable ECG, spun out of the University of Cambridge, will roll out across primary and secondary care and UK civil service departments. It holds UKCA marking and a US FDA 510(k) application is under way.

brefsEurope.title: MHRA adopts all 44 recommendations of the national commission on AI regulation in healthcare, with continuous device monitoring
brefsEurope.summary: An end to one-off pre-market assessment: guidance on AI device changes by December, a consultation on classification in early 2027, a roadmap by spring 2027; the AI Airlock sandbox reopens for applications (selections in November).

brefsIntl.title: Zenflow raises $52M Series D led by Cook Medical for its Spring implant for benign prostatic hyperplasia
brefsIntl.summary: ClavystBio, Invus Opportunities, F-Prime and Medtech Venture Partners also take part; the pivotal study shows 60% responders vs 33% for sham, with FDA approval in December 2025: a study-to-commercialization comparable for European urology implants.

word.full: Application-Specific Integrated Circuit for Neural Interfaces
word.fr: Application-Specific Integrated Circuit for Neural Interfaces
word.definition: A custom, ultra-low-power chip that amplifies and digitizes brain signals and drives stimulation, instead of generic electronics too bulky and power-hungry for an implant.

parts.label: Analog front end
parts.role: the ear: amplifies tiny neural signals

parts.label: Digital processing
parts.role: the sorter: filters and compresses data

how.t: Electrodes pick up signals of a few microvolts that the chip amplifies without drowning them in noise.
The chip digitizes, filters and reduces the data stream to fit an implant's power and heat budget.
It sends calibrated pulses to the electrodes and communicates wirelessly with the outside.

word.why: Every neurotech player faces the same bottleneck (channels, power, size): a reusable silicon building block becomes a scaling lever and an entry barrier, which is why investors are drawn to neural chip suppliers.

startups.name: MintNeuro

startups.name: Precision Neuroscience
startups.use: Layer 7 cortical interface (thin, flexible electrode array), FDA 510(k) clearance for 30-day use in 2025; $250M Series D in Sept 2026

startups.name: Neuralink
startups.use: N1 implant (1,024 electrodes on 64 threads) built on custom ASIC electronics, higher-volume production announced for 2026
